short: The sea cave beneath Tintagel Castle.
note: A sea cave beneath Tintagel in Cornwall, associated in local legend with Merlin. Tintagel’s Arthurian fame derives from medieval accounts of Arthur’s conception there.

sources.label: English Heritage: Tintagel Castle and Merlin’s Cave

short: The classical hero famed for his strength.
note: The Roman name of Greek Heracles, son of Zeus and Alcmena, renowned for his twelve labors and extraordinary strength.

short: The king whose fifty daughters bore Heracles’s children.
note: The king of Thespiae in Greek mythology who had fifty daughters and arranged for Heracles to father children with them.

short: Three mathematical laws of planetary motion.
note: Planets follow ellipses with the Sun at one focus; equal areas are swept out in equal times; and the square of an orbital period is proportional to the cube of the orbit’s semimajor axis.
